statement: Rao reports excavation during 1967–73 under Dibrugarh University's Anthropology department. The report places Sarutaru approximately 25 km southeast of Guwahati, on a small hillock at the Shillong plateau/Brahmaputra plain margin, with the Digaru river on the northern side. Rao distinguishes stratified Daojali Hading finds from earlier surface or household collections of celts.
evidence_status: Provisional research finding; verify before manuscript use

statement: Authors report OSL dating of excavated pottery: Daojali Hading sample LD1728 gives 2.7 ± 0.3 ka; Gawak Abri LD1727 gives 2.3 ± 0.2 ka. These are pottery luminescence estimates, not radiocarbon dates or proof of the earliest arrival of humans. Daojali Hading is in Dima Hasao, Assam; Gawak Abri is a Meghalaya comparison.
locator: Printed pp.492–496; Table 1 p.493; Figure 3 p.495.
evidence_status: Provisional research finding; verify before manuscript use

statement: Study analyzes seven charcoal samples, five potsherds and five sediment samples from test pits. Publisher abstract reports approximately 240–1379 CE for the analyzed material, despite Neolithic classification of a nearby reported site. Ground/polished axes, pottery and megaliths occur in the archaeological record of the valley.
locator: Abstract; supplementary material link listed, not downloaded
evidence_status: Provisional research finding; verify before manuscript use

statement: The study area lies in the Meghalaya plateau foothills; Sarutaru and Marakdola are its previously excavated sites. Indexed fieldwork passage says Marakdola, now Morogdula, was relocated using menhirs, but the old Sarutaru excavation spot remained untraceable. Modern roads, factories and residential development complicate relocation.
locator: Institutional abstract; indexed printed page 41 and Table 1.3
evidence_status: Provisional research finding; verify before manuscript use

statement: Author reports surface exploration of Bichikkri, Kekang-Adong and Langmet in western Karbi Anglong. Pottery similarities span Neolithic, early historic and medieval assemblages; chronology from fabric and decoration is difficult. Early historic assignment is comparative and provisional; locally reported stone tools at Kekang-Adong were not found during this survey.
locator: Methods p.671; Figures 1–6 pp.672–675; discussion pp.676–677.
evidence_status: Provisional research finding; verify before manuscript use

statement: ASI dates accidental discovery to 1969 and describes excavation between 1970 and 2003. Its joint 2008–09 excavation with Assam Directorate found brick steps leading to a tank, floors and hearths. Page reports earlier Sunga-Kushana-period cultural findings and several ceramic types, while also retaining the older medieval two-period scheme.
locator: Site narrative lines 59–68 in web extraction, particularly 2008–09 findings
evidence_status: Provisional research finding; verify before manuscript use

statement: Gauhati University researchers M. C. Goswami and T. C. Sharma explored central and northern Garo Hills. Report describes stone tools resembling palaeolithic choppers and scrapers; resemblance is a typological observation.
locator: Explorations and Excavations, ASSAM, section 7: Exploration in District Garo Hills; figure 1 mentioned in excerpt
evidence_status: Provisional research finding; verify before manuscript use

statement: A 1.5 m Sakali wetland sequence contains 34 NPP types. Five bulk sediment radiocarbon samples underpin an IntCal20/Bacon age model spanning roughly 4,100 calibrated years. The earliest zone is interpreted as warm/humid with woody vegetation. Grazing and agriculture proxies intensify particularly within the last 500 years; these cannot establish prehistoric rice domestication.
locator: Materials and methods: NPP extraction and chronology of sediment samples
NPP Zone I (150–100 cm, 4,040–2,260 cal yrs BP)
evidence_status: Provisional research finding; verify before manuscript use

statement: A 50 cm swamp core from Gauhati University yielded ten analysed samples and three pollen zones. Authors explicitly obtained no absolute dates and infer relative chronology through nearby archives. Cerealia and other pollen support their local agricultural interpretation, but cannot provide a securely dated prehistoric cultivation horizon.
locator: p.46 paragraph beginning The present study
evidence_status: Provisional research finding; verify before manuscript use

statement: The Dabaka Swamp 3.2 m core is interpreted as alternating fluvial and vegetation phases from 14,120 cal BP, including cool/dry conditions around the Younger Dryas and mixed deciduous forest later. The abstract links post-768 cal BP vegetation disturbance to settlement. Obtain full methods and dating table before treating phase boundaries as verified.
evidence_status: Provisional research finding; verify before manuscript use

statement: The field overview reports renewed examinations in 2014/2016 and comparisons with Laos. Its p.160 extract acknowledges unresolved dating and iron associations. Similar jar morphology is a comparative lead, not a measured Assam chronology or proof of one migration.
locator: Printed pp.151–162; discussion p.160; figures pp.154–160.
evidence_status: Provisional research finding; verify before manuscript use

statement: The 2020 Dima Hasao survey recorded four previously unreported jar sites, bringing the reported total to eleven, ten geolocated. This is documentation evidence. The accessible abstract provides no scientific dating result or burial excavation result.
evidence_status: Provisional research finding; verify before manuscript use

statement: Documents stone jars in Saipung, East Jaintia Hills. The historical salt-network connection is Colani's speculation, and earlier uses proposed for Assam included grinding or storage. Such interpretive variation is useful to show uncertainty rather than assert confirmed funerary function everywhere.
evidence_status: Provisional research finding; verify before manuscript use

statement: Forty-one boreholes along a 120 km transect distinguish Brahmaputra-Jamuna and Old Brahmaputra paleovalleys and infer repeated avulsions. This is downstream Bengal delta evidence. It illustrates river mobility methods but cannot date channel changes at an Assam settlement.
evidence_status: Provisional research finding; verify before manuscript use

statement: Rao describes three Sarutaru trenches with celts and pottery in one cultural horizon, and two Marakdola trenches with ceramic deposits. Sarutaru vessels are described as handmade; Marakdola vessels include kaolin fabrics and wheel manufacture. The article reports fieldwork in 1971–74, differing from the Man and Environment report’s 1967–73.
locator: pp.195–198 Sarutaru; p.199 Marakdola section; plates I–III; figures 2–6.
evidence_status: Provisional research finding; verify before manuscript use
